title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's preparatory notes for the 1981 'Longue Marche', on anabelian Galois theory. Here E_X^ξ denotes the (profinite étale) fundamental group of a 0-connected (connected) scheme X, based at a 'point' ξ.

On the previous page he defined E_X^ξ for a geometric point ξ, its functoriality for maps (X,ξ)→(Y,η), and (10) the kernel E_{X/Y}^{X̃} = Ker(E_X^{X̃} → E_Y^{X̃}). Here X̃ is a universal cover of X, used as base point; it also bases Y through X̃→Y, so E_Y^{X̃} = E_Y^{Ỹ}.

This page generalizes the base point.
- For connected X, any 1-connected (simply connected) T with a map T→X gives a fibre functor Z ↦ Hom_X(T,Z) on finite étale X-schemes. This yields a fundamental group E_X^T = π_1(X;T). Geometric points Spec Ω and pro-universal covers are special cases.
- For a triple T→X→Y with X, Y connected and T 1-connected, he sets (11) E^T_{X/Y} := Ker(E^T_X → E^T_Y). He notes this is functorial in such triples.
- Special cases: E_{X/Y} (T = X̃); E^Ω_{X/Y} (geometric point); E^{X̃}_{X/A} for Y = Spec A; E^{B̃}_{B/A} for an A-algebra B.
- Left margin (partly illegible): for variable T this is presumably essentially independent of T, up to inner automorphisms. A second note isolates the case where E^T_X → E^T_Y is an epimorphism.

Programme: 'what would be interesting is a universal homotopy exact sequence (in dim 1)' for X→Y. This means the SGA1-type sequence π_1(fibre) → π_1(X) → π_1(Y) holding after any base change. Then the datum of a 1-connected T→X (for X→Y given) can be interpreted as the datum of a 1-connected T→Y plus a lift T→X, i.e. a section of X_T = X ×_Y T → T. The next page confirms this.

The goal (next page) is (12) E^T_{X/Y} ≅ π_1(X_T;T) ≅ E^T_{X_T} and the short exact sequence (13) 1 → E^T_{X/Y} → E^T_X → E^T_Y → 1. The geometric fundamental group is thus identified with the fundamental group of the base change to a simply connected 'cover' of the base. This generalizes π_1(X_{K̄}) = Ker(π_1(X) → Gal(K̄/K)) for X geometrically connected over a field K. The motivation is to define the 'geometric' or arithmetic-relative fundamental group intrinsically, with flexible base points, for the anabelian programme.
errors: Not an error but a caveat: for B/A a finite separable extension of fields, Spec B → Spec A induces an injection on π_1, so E^{B̃}_{B/A} is trivial. The special case is only interesting for general rings or non-finite situations, or Grothendieck intends a different meaning.

Functoriality of E^T_{X/Y} 'in the triple' and independence from T hold only up to inner automorphisms (outer action). The page does not make this explicit, though the margin note seems to gesture at it.

The surjectivity E^T_X → E^T_Y needed for (13) requires a hypothesis, e.g. geometrically connected fibres or a proper separable morphism. The page flags this only in a margin note ('Cas où ... est épi').

ideas.what: Fundamental group based at an arbitrary simply connected T→X (fibre functor Hom_X(T,−)), generalizing geometric points and universal covers
ideas.modern_name: fibre functors / generalized base points (pro-universal cover, strictly henselian or 'tangential'-type base points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck SGA1 (fibre functors, pro-representability); later Deligne 1989 for tangential base points
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V (Galois categories, pro-representable fibre functors)

ideas.what: Relative fundamental group E^T_{X/Y} = Ker(π_1(X;T) → π_1(Y;T))
ideas.modern_name: geometric fundamental group / kernel in the fundamental exact sequence
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX Thm 6.1, Exp. X Cor. 1.4 (homotopy exact sequence)

ideas.what: Hypothesis of a 'universal' (base-change stable) homotopy exact sequence, letting E^T_{X/Y} be identified with π_1 of the base change X_T for 1-connected T→Y
ideas.modern_name: homotopy exact sequence stable under base change; identification π_1^{geom} = π_1(X ×_Y Ỹ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck SGA1 Exp. X; later refinements by e.g. Hoshi on exactness conditions
ideas.where_published: Essentially SGA1 Exp. X; formulation via 1-connected T unsure

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes setting up notation for relative and geometric fundamental groups with generalized base points and the SGA1 homotopy exact sequence. All of it is standard; the formulation via arbitrary 1-connected T is a mild notational flourish, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: First line: probably '(C'est un foncteur pour un triple' rather than '(Cela [?] un foncteur'.
'(en dim 2)' more likely reads '(en dim 1)', i.e. a homotopy exact sequence at the π_1 level.

'alors le dernier [?] (pour X = Y dernier [?]) de T → X' should likely read 'alors la donnée (pour X → Y donné) de T → X, (avec T 1-connexe) pourra s'interpréter par la donnée d'un ...'. This continues on the next page with 'T → Y et d'un relèvement en T → X'.
Margin bottom: 'Cas où E^T_X → E^T_Y est épi'.
Line '[?] un pt géom. de X' is probably 'Ω un pt géom. de X, E^Ω_{X/Y}'.
Line '[?] $(T \to X \to Y)$': the word above the parenthesis appears to be '(libre?)' or 'ébauché'; the sense is 'functor in (T→X→Y)'.
